{{Neutral}} [[Thorium Advance]] | affiliation = [[Dark Iron clan]], [[Thorium Brotherhood]], [[Independent]] | loc = Southern [[Khaz Modan]] | territory = Contested }} The '''Searing Gorge''' is a [[contested]] [[zone|region]] in southern [[Khaz Modan]]. It is home to a group of exceptionally stout [[Dark Iron dwarf|Dark Iron dwarves]] called the [[Thorium Brotherhood]], who have split from the [[Dark Iron clan]]. ==History== [[File:Dustfire Valley.jpg|thumb|Dustfire Valley.]] The Searing Gorge was presumably once a verdant valley, and a part of the [[Redridge Mountains]], until the landscape was obliterated in a massive explosion over 230 years ago. In the [[War of the Three Hammers]], the leader of the Dark Iron dwarves, [[Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan]], sought to summon a supernatural minion that would turn the tide of the war back to his favor. He and seven of his most trusted and powerful dwarves called upon the ancient powers sleeping beneath the world. To their surprise, the creature that emerged was more terrible than any nightmare they could have imagined: the ancient Firelord [[Ragnaros]].[[War of the Three Hammers (History of Warcraft)]] With the Firelord's awakening a new volcano, [[Blackrock Mountain]], erupted out of the mountain ridge, forever blackening the surrounding lands and reducing the Dark Iron capital of [[Ruins of Thaurissan|Thaurissan]] to rubble. The steppes to the south came to be known as the [[Burning Steppes]], and the ravaged valley to the north the Searing Gorge. Upon completion of their new [[Shadowforge City|capital city]], the Dark Iron sought control of land for their filthy, industrious works. They looked directly to the gorge north of their mountain, and turned their focus to a very large scale digging operation at the bottom of the blackened valley. The giant excavation site came to be known as [[the Cauldron]],[[The Smoldering Ruins of Thaurissan]] and within, the [[Slag Pit]] was settled as an underground mining site rich with multiple [[ore]]s. The labor was mainly done by [[slave]]s, who were for the most part of captured enemies. ===World of Warcraft=== {{Wow-section}} At some point, the [[Thorium Brotherhood]], a group of [[Dark Iron dwarf|Dark Iron dwarves]] who left the [[Dark Iron clan]], established [[Thorium Point]] as their base of operations in the region. Overlooking the region called the [[Cauldron]], they kept a close eye on the Dark Iron dwarves' activities.[[Game Guide/Classic Reputation#Thorium Brotherhood]] The [[Stonewrought Pass]] remained locked down for many years, guarded by one [[Mountaineer Pebblebitty]] in recent days. The mountaineers turned away anyone seeking passage, so adventurers trying to enter the gorge could only come by way of either the [[Blackrock Spire]] or the [[Badlands]] trail south of [[Kargath]]. The adventurer was eventually rewarded a [[Key to Searing Gorge]][[At Last!]] by [[Curator Thorius]] of [[Ironforge]] for killing a kodo named [[Margol the Rager]],[[The Horn of the Beast]] the bane of every archaeologist that ever set foot in the Searing Gorge.[[Proof of Deed (quest)]] ===The Burning Crusade=== {{Bc-section}} Prior to the start of the [[invasion of Outland]], the Searing Gorge was invaded by a group of [[Burning Legion]] [[demon]]s led by [[Highlord Kruul]].[[Dark Portal Opens]] ===Cataclysm=== {{Cata-section}} The events of the [[Cataclysm (event)|Cataclysm]] prompted the mountaineers to unlock the passage and begin allowing adventurers to travel at their own risk... Mountaineer Pebblebitty remains, still trying to turn adventurers away. ==Geography== ===Maps and subregions=== [[File:WorldMap-SearingGorge.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Map of Searing Gorge.]] [[File:WorldMap-SearingGorge-1.5.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Map of Searing Gorge prior to ''[[World of Warcraft: Cataclysm|Cataclysm]]''.]] {| class="darktable hlist" |- | *[[Blackchar Cave]] *[[Blackrock Mountain]] *[[Cauldron|The Cauldron]] **[[Slag Pit|The Slag Pit]] *[[Dustfire Valley]] *[[Firewatch Ridge]] *[[Grimesilt Dig Site]] *[[Iron Summit]] *[[Pyrox Flats]] *[[Sea of Cinders|The Sea of Cinders]] *[[Stonewrought Pass]] *{{replaced|Tanner Camp}} *[[Thorium Advance]] *[[Thorium Point]] |- || ---- ;{{RPG-inline}} [[Warcraft RPG]] *[[Altar of Storms (Burning Steppes)|Altar of Storms]] |} File:WorldMap-SearingGorge-old.jpg|Map of Searing Gorge prior to [[patch 1.5]]. {{clear|left}} ===Dungeons and raids=== There are actually no instances in the Searing Gorge. However, [[Blackrock Mountain]] lies between it and the [[Burning Steppes]]. It is home to [[Blackrock Depths]] (level 52-60 dungeon), [[Blackrock Spire]] (level 54-60 dungeon), [[Molten Core]] (level 60 raid), [[Blackwing Lair]] (level 60 raid), [[Blackrock Caverns]] (level 80-83 dungeon){{cata-inline}}, and [[Blackwing Descent]] (level 85 raid){{cata-inline}}. ===Travel hubs=== ====={{Neutral}} [[Flight path]]s from [[Thorium Point]]===== *{{Alliance}} [[Stormwind]], [[Elwynn Forest]] *{{Alliance}} [[Ironforge]], [[Dun Morogh]] *{{Alliance}} [[Thelsamar]], [[Loch Modan]] *{{Horde}} [[New Kargath]], [[Badlands]] *{{Neutral}} [[Iron Summit]], Searing Gorge *{{Alliance}} [[Morgan's Vigil]], [[Burning Steppes]] *{{Horde}} [[Flame Crest]], [[Burning Steppes]] ====={{Neutral}} [[Flight path]]s from [[Iron Summit]]===== *{{Neutral}} [[Thorium Point]], Searing Gorge *{{Neutral}} [[Flamestar Post]], [[Burning Steppes]] ===Adjacent regions=== {| class="darktable" |- ! Zone Name || Faction || Level Range || Direction || Access subzone || Access method |- | [[Loch Modan]] || {{Alliance}} | 10 - 60 || Northeast || [[Stonewrought Pass]] | By foot through the Stonewrought Pass |- | [[Badlands|The Badlands]] | {{Alliance}}{{Horde}} | 40 - 60 || West || | By foot {{coords|1|62|Badlands}} or by Horde flightpath from Thorium Point to Kargath |- | [[Blackrock Mountain]] | {{Alliance}}{{Horde}} | 40 - 60 || South || [[Blackrock Mountain]] | By foot |- | [[Burning Steppes]] | {{Alliance}} {{Horde}} | 40 - 60 || South || [[Blackrock Mountain]] | By foot through Blackrock Mountain or by flightpath from Thorium Point to Morgan's Vigil or Flame Crest |} ==Notable characters== [[File:Tanner Camp.jpg|thumb|Tanner Camp.]] {{Main|Searing Gorge NPCs}} Searing Gorge is home to several characters of note. At Thorium Point, [[Hansel Heavyhands]] seeks aid in the battle against the golems, spiders, and incendosaurs of the region. [[Master Smith Burninate]] attempts to create fiery flux with the help of trustworthy individuals. And from his guarded spot nearby, [[Velarok Windblade]] sends bold adventurers into the holdings of the Dark Irons in an attempt to burn down all of their sentry towers. ==Quests== {{Main|Searing Gorge storyline}} ==Resources== *[[Herb]]s **[[Firebloom]] **[[Sungrass]] *[[Ore]] **[[Gold Vein]] **[[Mithril Deposit]] **[[Truesilver Deposit]] ==Wild creatures== *[[Fire elemental]]s *[[Golem]]s *[[Incendosaur]]s *[[Lava elemental]]s *[[Felsteed]]s *[[Spider]]s *[[Thunder lizard]]s ==Before ''Cataclysm''== Prior to ''[[World of Warcraft: Cataclysm|Cataclysm]]'', the Alliance entrance to the Searing Gorge in Loch Modan was locked. Players had to obtain the [[Key to Searing Gorge]] via a questline culminating in [[At Last!]], although rogues with lockpicking of 225 could simply pick the doors, and players (especially Horde) could always enter through the Badlands. With the Cataclysm, the key and the quest to obtain it have been removed, and the entrance is now unlocked. The zone was also changed from a level 43 - 52 zone to one suited to level 47 - 51 characters. ==In the RPG== {{RPG-section}} The '''Searing Gorge''' might be a poor first sight for visitors to [[Khaz Modan]]. A shattered, desolate area, the Searing Gorge is the northern equivalent of the [[Burning Steppes]]. The only road connecting Khaz Modan and [[Azeroth (continent)|Azeroth]] passes through here, so those wishing to make the journey must trek across this barren landscape. No government holds sway in the Searing Gorge and no settlements exist within its confines. The area has no resources, so no armies have bothered with it. Nevertheless, the land can be interesting for an explorer who leaves the road. Many beasts hide in the surrounding rocks and crags, waiting to ambush the unwary traveler. The weary traveler can instead ambush them. Desolate but not lifeless, the Searing Gorge hosts dangers and secrets aplenty. ===History=== 300 years ago when the [[Dark Iron clan|Dark Irons]] summoned [[Ragnaros]] it caused a volcanic explosion that devastated the surrounding land, including the Burning Steppes to the south. Since that time, the region has been the wasteland that it is today. No people call the Searing Gorge home, though the land falls within Khaz Modan and therefore is under the purview of the [[Ironforge (kingdom)|Ironforge]] [[Dwarf|dwarves]]. The dwarves have many other worries at the moment, so odds are the Searing Gorge will remain untamed for years to come, especially since there is little to no reason to reclaim it. A group of [[Stonegullet]] [[ogre]]s barricades the road leading south to Blackrock Spire, demanding tribute from all wishing to pass — and the three [[black drake]]s with them ensure that all travelers pay the toll. ===Geography=== The Searing Gorge is barren and hot. The ground is scarred with fissures and dotted with broken rock, the weather hot and dry. It lies south of [[Dun Morogh]], west of the [[Badlands]], and immediately north of [[Blackrock Spire]] and the [[Burning Steppes]]. Shattered crags and jagged chasms are the only features of note, and few landmarks exist off the road to guide a straying traveler. [[Rock golem]]s and [[Dark Iron dwarf|Dark Iron dwarves]] roam it. No settlements stand here, and few important sites exist. The journey from Khaz Modan to Azeroth (and vice versa) is long and dangerous.''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 78 - 79''[[World of Warcraft: The Roleplaying Game]]'', pg. 17 ==Notes and trivia== *Players taking the flight to Ironforge from Stormwind can observe many subzones of this area. *If you were to die in one of the Blackrock Mountain instances, it would take you to the Thorium Point graveyard. It is convenient as it is not far from the [[flight point]]. *[[The Charred Oak]] was once located here, overlooking the [[Cauldron]]. ==Gallery== File:The Sea of Cinders.jpg|The Sea of Cinders.
